items.excerpt: Pixelsncodes released Lumen, a free open-source Windows synth built with the Claude AI coding agent, featuring an image-to-wavetable engine that reads any dropped image's bytes and turns them into playable wavetables.

In his first formal interview in a decade, Skrillex argues AI songs can go viral but can't deliver the feeling of being seen by a human creator, laying out how he thinks producers should position their craft against algorithmic music.

Analytics firm Viberate launched an official MCP server that lets Claude, ChatGPT and other AI assistants query its data on 11M artists, 100M songs and 19M playlists in natural language — turning stats into lineup suggestions and marketing strategies as part of an 'AI-first' pivot.

Ableton soft-launched Learn, an interactive browser-based music education platform powered by the engine behind Note and Move — deliberately positioned so beginners build real production skills 'instead of prompting AI or something.'

The Atlantic's AI Watchdog project released four searchable databases covering 20M+ songs used to train Suno, Udio and Google's Lyria — letting producers check if their own tracks are in the training sets, with artist Hainbach finding 151 of his songs in one dataset.

Australia's leading music and creative organisations launched a united campaign demanding federal copyright protections after local songs were allegedly used to train AI models without consent, calling it 'the largest theft of intellectual property in our history.'

Hypebot examines whether audiences genuinely oppose AI in music creation or whether the backlash mirrors the resistance that met every past technology shift in production — a question shaping how openly working musicians disclose AI use.

Sound designer Fabio Gotti details building his debut HydraTek plugin Erebos as a deliberately human-made product, warning that audio tools and marketing 'can quickly collapse into generic AI-generated aesthetics' — a counterpoint craft story to the vibe-coded plugin wave.
The Quantum MIDI Sequencer is a generative music sequencer that translates nuclear radiation events into MIDI notes, turning true physical randomness into an algorithmic composition source.
